topics.name: Appendix 2 Grammar: nouns, pronouns and determiners
points: Feminine and plural noun formation; infinitives used as nouns
Articles: agreement, l' before vowels, functions and omissions; de after negatives and quantities
Partitive articles with uncountable nouns; definite article before an adjective to form a noun (HT)
Demonstrative, possessive, interrogative and indefinite adjectives; negative aucun(e) (HT)
Subject, direct and indirect object, reflexive and emphatic pronouns; relative qui
y and en; further object and emphatic pronouns; personne ne / rien ne; relative où and que (HT)

topics.name: Appendix 2 Grammar: verbs
points: Negation: ne…pas, ne…jamais, ne…rien, ne…personne; ne…plus, ne…ni…ni, ne…pas encore, ne…que (HT)
Interrogatives: intonation, est-ce que, question word + inversion
Present passive using par
Impersonal verbs: il y a/avait/aura, weather, il faut, time; il est + adjective + de, il vaut mieux (HT)
Reflexive verbs (reflexive and reciprocal meanings) in all tenses
être en train de and venir de
Present tense: regular verbs and aller, avoir, être, faire, mettre; depuis + present (HT)
Modal verbs devoir, pouvoir, savoir, vouloir + infinitive
Perfect tense and past participle agreement
Imperfect tense: habitual and continuous actions
Periphrastic future (aller + infinitive) and inflectional future (HT)
Conditional: vouloir (would like); conditional of regular -er verbs and key irregulars (HT)
Imperative, including 'let's' forms (HT)
Present participle after en (HT)

topics.name: Appendix 2 Grammar: adjectives, adverbs, prepositions and derivational morphology
points: Adjectives: gender, number and position
Comparative and superlative adjectives
Adverbs: position; comparatives and superlatives (le mieux, le pire)
Prepositions: à/de after verbs and adjectives, en/à with places, contractions, de for possession
pour/sans + infinitive; avant de + infinitive; après avoir + past participle (HT)
Derivational morphology: in-/im- prefixes, -ième, -able, -ion/-ation; -eur/-ateur and -ment adverbs (HT)
Sound-symbol correspondences (SSCs) for reading aloud and dictation
